correctness.rationale: The event T_r<k<=T_{r+1} has exactly one previously earliest r-occupancy winner that remains at r; the next iid uniform mark hits it with probability 1/m, proving the exact joint mass [S_{r+1}(k)-S_r(k)]/m including endpoint k. Summing gives P(B_r)=(ET_{r+1}-ET_r)/m, and rate-m Poissonization with m independent rate-one clocks gives its absolutely convergent integral. For fixed r, Taylor expansion Q_s(x)=1-x^s/s!+O(x^{s+1}), integrated with an exponential dominating envelope, gives E Z_s=c_s m^{-1/s}+O_s(m^{-2/s}); the difference yields the displayed two-scale expansion. The joint kernel, T_{r+1}/m^{r/(r+1)} Weibull limit and negligible ET_r at this scale yield an integrated-tail conditional Weibull density via Riemann sums and tightness. Independent exact enumeration of all finite uniform sequences until threshold for (m,r)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3), including every conditional k and total probability 13/16, 175/243, 27/32, reproduces the identity. Finite cases are not asymptotic proof.
